context_pill: PGBP Computation & Total Income of ILT Limited
example_summary: Computation of total income for ILT Limited for AY 2026-27 starting from a net profit of ₹ 405 lacs, incorporating adjustments for Section 28(iv), Section 41(1), Section 43B, Section 40(a)(i), Rule 6DD(i), and Section 80GGB.
source_provision:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Business Income & Deductions

| Statutory Provision | Nature of Transaction / Item | Core Statutory Condition | Tax Treatment / Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 28(iv)** | Benefit or Perquisite | Value of any benefit or perquisite arising from business, whether convertible into money or not | Taxable as business income under Section 28(iv) |
| **Section 41(1)** | Remission or Cessation of Trading Liability | Allowance or deduction was made in past years in respect of loss, expenditure, or trading liability | Deemed income in the year of remission or cessation, irrespective of accounting entry or running account status |
| **Section 43B** | Conversion of Arrear Interest into Loan | Interest due to scheduled banks is allowed only on actual payment; conversion into a fresh loan is not actual payment | Disallowed at conversion; actual payment of funded loan instalments is allowed as deduction |
| **Section 40(a)(i)** | Interest Payable Outside India | Tax must be deducted at source and deposited on or before the due date of filing return under Section 139(1) | Fully allowed if TDS is deposited within the statutory due date under Section 139(1) |
| **Section 40A(3) & Rule 6DD(i)** | Cash Payments for Salary | Cash payments exceeding statutory limits attract disallowance unless covered by specified exceptions | Allowed if employee is temporarily posted for a continuous period of more than 15 days in a non-normal place of duty |
| **Section 80GGB** | Contribution to Electoral Trust | Contribution made by an Indian company to an electoral trust by any mode other than cash | Allowed as deduction from Gross Total Income under Chapter VI-A |


> [!IMPORTANT] Section 43B Rule on Funded Interest:
> Conversion of unpaid interest into a fresh loan or funded interest does not amount to actual payment. Deduction is permitted only when the instalments of the funded interest are actually paid to the financial institution.


> [!NOTE] Rule 6DD(i) Exception:
> Cash payments of salary made to an employee stationed temporarily for a continuous period exceeding 15 days outside their normal place of duty are expressly protected from Section 40A(3) disallowance.

director.justification: The question requires computing the total business income and total income of ILT Limited by adjusting net profit for various statutory add-backs and deductions under Sections 28(iv), 41(1), 43B, 40(a)(i), 40A(3), and 80GGB.
director.visual_metaphor: An interactive tax computation ledger sheet reconciling profit and loss entries with Income Tax Act adjustments.

beat_plan.beat_goal: Establish the starting point of net profit and state the overall objective of computing total income for ILT Limited.
Demonstrate the add-back of perquisites under Section 28(iv) and deemed income from waiver under Section 41(1).
Illustrate Section 43B rule where conversion of unpaid interest into loan is disallowed, but actual payment of funded instalments is allowed.
Show that interest paid to foreign company is allowed as deduction since TDS was deposited before Section 139(1) due date.
Explain the cash salary exception under Rule 6DD(i) protecting payments from Section 40A(3) disallowance due to continuous temporary posting over 15 days.
Detail the tax treatment of electoral trust contribution: disallowed under PGBP but allowed as deduction under Section 80GGB.
Summarize the step-by-step PGBP computation arriving at final total income.
